testimonial.author: Head of Operations

menorcaHotelChain.problem: Four properties, 400+ employees, a decade of growth piling up tools: PMS, booking engine, channel manager, department-level CRMs, critical spreadsheets owned by a single person. No one had the full list of what the chain used, paid for, or depended on. Leadership wanted to roll out AI but didn't know on what foundation.
menorcaHotelChain.context:
When the PMS doesn't talk directly to the channel manager, someone does it by hand. When each department has its own CRM and none consolidates the guest history, marketing campaigns fire without real data. When only one person knows how the rate connector works, that person can't take a vacation.

Every manual integration is hours. Every unused SaaS license is money. Every single-owner system is an operational risk. Before adding new layers of automation or AI, leadership needs to know exactly what they're building on.
menorcaHotelChain.engineeringIntro: We applied the Digital X-Ray methodology: kick-off, structured interviews with 12 functional areas, document collection (SaaS contracts, billing, accesses), real integration mapping, and per-system risk analysis. We cross-checked declarations against logs and billing to surface Shadow IT.
menorcaHotelChain.impact: 47 applications inventoried (12 without a clear owner), 23% of SaaS spend flagged as redundant or unused, 3 critical key-person dependencies documented, and an executive plan for the next 12 months.
menorcaHotelChain.iaReadiness: Every AI project starts with data. If data is fragmented across silos, duplicated between systems, or managed by hand in spreadsheets, the AI model will reproduce those problems at speed and scale. The Digital X-Ray is not just an audit — it's the map that turns a hotel chain into an organization ready to automate.

faq.q: How long does a Digital X-Ray take?
faq.a: The full project runs 3 weeks: kick-off and access setup, interviews across 12 functional areas, data analysis and cross-checking, and a final executive session with the report. We do not interrupt hotel operations.

faq.q: How much does a hotel technology audit cost?
faq.a: Each Digital X-Ray is scoped based on the size of the chain and number of properties. Request a proposal to receive a detailed estimate within 48 hours.

faq.q: How is this different from a cybersecurity audit?
faq.a: A cybersecurity audit looks for vulnerabilities and attack vectors. The Digital X-Ray maps the full operational technology stack: what systems exist, how they integrate, what SaaS is being paid for, what Shadow IT runs without IT's knowledge, and what needs to be resolved before scaling or implementing AI.

faq.q: What happens after the audit?
faq.a: The executive report includes a prioritized 12-month plan. If you choose, IA Operators can support implementation with a Technology Roadmap or begin automation projects directly on the already-mapped stack.

faq.q: Do we need an audit before implementing AI in the hotel?
faq.a: Yes. Without a complete inventory of systems and documented integrations, any AI project will build on assumptions. The result is integrations that don't work, inconsistent data, and projects that don't scale. The Digital X-Ray is the safe starting point.

tourBooking.problem: Tour and experience companies lose revenue when users ask for price and availability and don’t get an immediate answer. The real challenge isn’t “chatting well” — it’s computing the correct price every time, because it changes by boat, season, experience, duration and number of guests.
tourBooking.engineeringIntro: We designed this system as a reliable agent: instead of throwing a spreadsheet into a prompt, we turned pricing rules into deterministic tools (code) and used AI only to understand intent, collect variables, and drive the conversation.
tourBooking.impact: Price quotes in seconds with deterministic pricing and a guided WhatsApp booking flow, reducing operational errors and first-contact manual workload.

propiziare.seoTitle: Propiziare Immigra — trilingual site and technical SEO | IA Operators
propiziare.title: Propiziare Immigra — trilingual site for an immigration advisory
propiziare.h1: Trilingual site and technical SEO for an immigration advisory
propiziare.subtitle: Spanish visas and residency · pt-BR · es · en
propiziare.tagline: A lead-capture site for a visa consultancy whose audience researches from Brazil, on mobile, on unreliable connections. Not a single third-party tag blocking first render.

gallery.heroAlt: Propiziare Immigra — Spanish visa and residency advisory

propiziare.problem: An immigration advisory competes in SERPs crowded with content farms, forums and law firms holding twenty-year-old domains. The visitor arrives at a high-stakes moment, moving country, and arrives on mobile, often on Brazilian mobile data. Every second before the first content is a consultation that leaves for another tab. The sector also carries a trust problem: someone searching for a Spanish digital nomad visa has already seen half a dozen pages promising the same thing without saying who answers.
propiziare.context: The audience is genuinely trilingual, not trilingual out of politeness: Brazilians researching in Portuguese, residents already in Spain comparing in Spanish, and international profiles arriving in English. That makes hreflang infrastructure rather than a footer ornament.
propiziare.engineeringIntro: The site was built on one hard rule: no third parties in the critical path. No tag manager, no embedded chat widget, no blocking remote fonts. Lead capture goes to WhatsApp through a direct link instead of an SDK, and analytics is not paid for with the visitor's load time. The rest is familiar discipline: static output served from a CDN, brotli compression, modern image formats with deferred loading below the fold, and a single canonical version per language with reciprocal hreflang.
propiziare.impact: The result is a site that renders its main content in under two seconds on simulated mobile and shifts nothing while loading. Lighthouse's three untimed categories — accessibility, best practices and SEO — sit at 100 on both mobile and desktop. The concrete numbers, with their date and method, are below.
whatItDoes: Explains each route in: student, digital nomad, work, non-lucrative, family reunification and arraigo
Captures qualified enquiries through a pre-consultation form with a direct WhatsApp handoff
Serves three languages with reciprocal hreflang and one canonical per version
Marks up the entity with organisation and advisor-person schema
Publishes supporting content on living in Spain after approval
howItWorks: Content architecture by intent: one page per visa route, not a generic services page
Static rendering served from a CDN, with brotli and cache headers
Zero third-party JavaScript in the critical path, so main-thread blocking stays flat
Modern image formats, deferred loading only below the fold
hreflang pt-BR / es / en plus x-default, reciprocal in all three directions

trilingual.title: Genuinely trilingual, not translated on top
trilingual.description: Three versions with their own canonical and reciprocal hreflang. Without it, Google picks which version a Brazilian sees, and it usually picks wrong.
bullets: pt-BR, es and en, plus x-default
One canonical per language, no orphan versions
Content adapted to the reader, not a literal translation of the Spanish

noThirdParty.title: Zero third parties in the critical path
noThirdParty.description: The most profitable engineering decision in the project. A typical tag manager costs 150 to 270 kB of JavaScript the visitor downloads before reading anything.
bullets: No tag manager and no embedded chat SDK
Lead capture through a direct WhatsApp link, not a widget
Main-thread blocking flat on desktop and minimal on mobile

entity.title: The entity marked up, not just the pages
entity.description: In a sector where the search engine weighs who signs the advice, declaring the organisation and the person advising is part of the SEO work, not an add-on.
bullets: Organisation and person schema linked to each other
Consistent authorship signals across all three language versions

security: The pre-consultation form collects the minimum needed to call back: name, contact and route of interest.
The conversation continues on WhatsApp, off the site, with no consultation history stored on the front end.
No third-party tags also means no silent data collection by scripts we do not control.

faq.q: Why give up Google Tag Manager?
faq.a: Because its cost is not zero and the visitor pays it. On comparable sites we have measured 150 to 270 kB of JavaScript from the tag container alone, with roughly half of it never executing. For an audience arriving on mobile data, that turns into seconds before the first content. When the client needs measurement, lightweight server-side analytics can be added without handing that weight back to the browser.

faq.q: Doesn't the language switcher take care of hreflang?
faq.a: No. The switcher is navigation for people; hreflang is a declaration to the search engine about which version belongs to which audience, and it has to be reciprocal: each version lists itself and every equivalent. Without reciprocity Google ignores the set and decides on its own.

faq.q: Do these scores hold over time?
faq.a: Not automatically. They degrade the moment someone adds a widget, a remote font or a campaign tag. That is why we publish the measurement date and method next to the number, and re-measure instead of keeping a screenshot.

hotelRevenue.seoTitle: Hotel Revenue Operator: validating a direct-booking product for hotels | IA Operators
hotelRevenue.title: Hotel Revenue Operator: direct bookings for independent hotels
hotelRevenue.h1: Validating a direct-booking product before building it
hotelRevenue.subtitle: Independent hotels in Spain · Phase 1
hotelRevenue.tagline: A landing page, a revenue calculator and pilot sign-ups to test whether a hotel would pay to win bookings back from the OTAs, before writing a single line of the assistant.
hotelRevenue.problem: An independent hotel pays commission on every booking that comes through an OTA such as Booking or Expedia, and many of those bookings start with a question its website did not answer in time. Building an assistant that answers and sends guests to the booking engine is technically manageable. The expensive part is building it and then finding out hotels will not pay for it.
hotelRevenue.context: The product hypothesis has four parts: the hotel loses direct bookings to unanswered questions, an assistant that answers and hands off to the booking engine wins some of them back, extras offered at the right moment add revenue, and the hotel pays if it can see the attribution. Phase 1 exists to test whether that holds up with real hotels, not to prove the software works.
hotelRevenue.engineeringIntro: Phase 1 is deliberately small: an indexable landing page, a revenue calculator on its own page and a form that stores the lead together with the calculation behind it. There is no chatbot, no login, no integrations and no payments. What there is, is rigour in what gets measured: the calculation lives in versioned pure functions, the server always repeats it instead of trusting the browser, and analytics carry no personal data.
hotelRevenue.impact: The product moves from idea to measurable experiment. Each lead arrives with the hotel's data, the chosen scenario and the formula version, so the diagnostic call is about concrete numbers and can ask directly whether the hotel would accept a pilot and at what price. Phase 2, the working assistant, only gets built if those answers justify it.

Shows three scenarios (conservative, realistic and potential) and states their limitations

honest.description: The page states that the savings are gross, that there is no seasonality and that the scenario percentages are working hypotheses, not industry averages.
bullets: Indicative-estimate notice always visible

faq.q: Why is there no chatbot yet?
faq.a: Because the first thing to prove is that there is a hotel willing to pay for it. Building the assistant, the booking-engine integrations and the attribution takes weeks. Measuring interest takes days. If Phase 1 does not land pilots, that time has been saved.

faq.q: Where do the scenario percentages come from?
faq.a: They are working hypotheses, and the page says so. They are not industry averages or client results. They let the hotel see a range based on its own data, not a promised figure.

faq.q: Why is the calculator not indexed?
faq.a: The same tool sits inside the landing page. Two indexable URLs with the same functional content would split the search traffic. The separate page serves as a destination for ads and direct links.

rgpdOps.seoTitle: RGPD Ops Starter: data protection as an ongoing operation | IA Operators
rgpdOps.title: RGPD Ops Starter: GDPR as an operation, not a folder
rgpdOps.h1: A tool for keeping data protection up to date
rgpdOps.subtitle: Spanish SMEs that win customers online · One-off payment
rgpdOps.tagline: A paid workspace where an SME keeps its processing activities, suppliers, rights requests, incidents and evidence up to date, with export of a draft Record of Processing Activities (RoPA).
rgpdOps.problem: An SME that wins customers through a website, WhatsApp, a CRM, a newsletter and tracking pixels builds up processing activities and suppliers without noticing. GDPR is usually dealt with once, with a set of templates, and then nobody updates them. When an access request or a breach arrives, there is no record of what data exists, where it is or who is responsible.
rgpdOps.context: The market offers two extremes: generic documents that end up in a drawer, or legal advice that a small SME cannot pay for every quarter. Something in between was needed: a tool that organises day-to-day operations and says clearly when a professional is required.
rgpdOps.engineeringIntro: RGPD Ops is a server-side workspace, not a form in the browser. Every change goes through SQL functions that only accept tables and columns from a closed list, always filter by the session's workspace and record the change in an audit log that cannot be edited. Access is bought through Stripe and delivered by magic link, with no passwords.
rgpdOps.impact: The SME goes from loose documents to a living record: eight modules with their due dates, a task plan with evidence, a guided quarterly review and the option to export everything as CSV and JSON. It also knows what the tool does not do: it gives no legal advice, certifies nothing and does not decide whether a breach must be notified.
whatItDoes: Records processing activities and generates a draft Record of Processing Activities (RoPA)
Organises suppliers, data collection points, rights requests and incidents
Proposes an action plan with tasks, owners by role and evidence
Guides a quarterly review and shows the maturity level by area

minimization.description: A data protection tool cannot become one more place where personal data piles up. That is why it has no fields for data subjects' names or documents.
bullets: Free text rejects emails, phone numbers and DNI/NIE numbers
Owners by role, evidence by reference, no file uploads
No AI on the workspace content

limits.title: Stated limits
limits.description: The tool does not decide legal bases or whether a DPIA is needed. When it detects signs of higher risk, it recommends a professional review instead of improvising an answer.
bullets: It is not legal advice or certification
A free diagnostic first to check whether it fits

security: Every private request checks again in the database that the order is paid, active and within its term.
The workspace ID always comes from the session: someone else's ID returns a 404.
Logs with closed fields, no email, token, IP or content. Workspaces are purged 90 days after access ends.

metrics.label: AI on your data
metrics.note: None: the workspace content is never sent to models

faq.q: Does it replace a lawyer or a DPO?
faq.a: No. It organises day-to-day operations and produces drafts, but it does not decide legal bases, does not determine whether a DPIA or a DPO is needed and does not decide whether a breach is notified to the AEPD. When there are signs of risk, it says so and recommends a professional review.

faq.q: Why does it not use AI?
faq.a: Because the workspace content describes how a company processes personal data. Sending it to an external model would add one more processor for no reason. The guidance and alerts are written, reviewed rules.

faq.q: What happens when the year of access ends?
faq.a: Everything can be exported as JSON and CSV at any time. After access ends, the workspace is kept for 90 days for export and then deleted.

rutaNacionalidad.seoTitle: Ruta Nacionalidad: private area for Spanish nationality by residence | IA Operators
rutaNacionalidad.title: Ruta Nacionalidad: the nationality application, saved and supported
rutaNacionalidad.h1: From a free calculator to an application followed step by step
rutaNacionalidad.subtitle: Spanish nationality by residence · es · pt-BR
rutaNacionalidad.tagline: A private area that saves the nationality calculator result, turns the case into a dated document checklist and prepares for the CCSE test, with an optional review by a specialist.
rutaNacionalidad.serviceType: Digital product for Spanish nationality by residence
rutaNacionalidad.problem: Applying for Spanish nationality by residence is a long process: the waiting period depends on the country of origin, residence has to be legal and continuous, there are exams and a list of documents that expire. Most people do the calculation once on a website, close the tab and come back months later with no idea where they stand.
rutaNacionalidad.context: Ruta Nacionalidad was built alongside the Propiziare Immigra website, whose audience researches in Spanish and Portuguese. The public calculator already answered the first question, when they could apply. What was missing was the next step: saving that result and supporting the application until it is submitted.
rutaNacionalidad.engineeringIntro: The product is split into two parts. The calculator lives on the public website, works without sign-up and runs the calculation in the browser, applying the periods in article 22 of the Spanish Civil Code. The private area is a separate, non-indexed application where users sign in with their email and a code, with no password, and save their case. Paid access is activated only when Stripe confirms the charge, not when the user returns from the payment page.
rutaNacionalidad.impact: What used to be a one-off calculation becomes an application with a status: dated documents, a calendar, a CCSE study plan, reminders and recalculation when the user's data or the rules change. Anyone who needs more than guidance can add a written review of their case by an immigration specialist.

Turns the case into a document checklist with statuses and dates
Organises a calendar and a study plan for the CCSE test

faq.a: No. It applies the Civil Code periods to the user's answers and gives an indicative date. It does not check any public register, and the grant is decided by the Ministry of Justice.

faq.a: Because they do different jobs. The public website has to load fast and rank; the private area stores personal data, must not be indexed and needs sessions and payments. Keeping them apart stops one from dragging the other down.

unRato.seoTitle: Un Rato: plumbing in Málaga via WhatsApp with AI and human review | IA Operators
unRato.title: Un Rato: home repairs in Málaga, starting with a WhatsApp message
unRato.h1: A plumbing service that starts and ends on WhatsApp
unRato.subtitle: Málaga city · Plumbing · Validation phase
unRato.tagline: The customer sends a message with a photo, the AI classifies the fault, a person approves the price and a verified local tradesperson is found. Nothing to download and no ringing round five companies.
unRato.problem: Finding a plumber for a dripping tap is harder than it should be: calls nobody answers, quotes that never arrive and prices you only learn at the end. For the self-employed tradesperson, the problem is the reverse: jobs come in with no photo, no address and no idea whether the customer will accept the price.
unRato.engineeringIntro: Un Rato runs on the official WhatsApp API, n8n and Postgres. The AI has a narrow role: it writes the conversation, extracts the data and classifies the fault from up to three photos. The decisions that matter are not its to make. Status changes are decided by deterministic code, the price comes from a catalogue and a person approves it from Telegram before it reaches the customer.
unRato.impact: Today, WhatsApp intake, photo classification, human price review and tradesperson onboarding are all live. Automatic assignment to a tradesperson is not yet: the offer and confirmation templates are under review at Meta and, in the meantime, the operator gets an alert to find one. The system already measures what will be needed to decide whether to scale: time to first response, price held and bot accuracy against the operator.

psicoSprint.seoTitle: PsicoSprint: adaptive psychometric test practice for Spanish civil-service exams | IA Operators
psicoSprint.title: PsicoSprint: adaptive psychometric test practice for Spanish civil-service exams
psicoSprint.h1: Psychometric practice with a plan that adjusts to every answer
psicoSprint.subtitle: Civil-service exams for the National Police, Guardia Civil and the Army
psicoSprint.tagline: A psychometric practice platform with a free level test, results by skill and a deterministic adaptive engine that adjusts difficulty and revisits mistakes.
psicoSprint.problem: Candidates preparing for a civil-service exam with psychometric tests usually practise with fixed question sets: they repeat what they already know, do not know which skill they are failing and have no way of measuring progress. Academies solve part of the problem, but at a price and on a timetable that do not suit everyone.
psicoSprint.engineeringIntro: PsicoSprint draws a clear line between what the AI does and what it does not. The question bank was drafted with help from a model, offline, and reviewed before publication. The engine that picks the next question is deterministic: it estimates mastery of each skill, raises or lowers difficulty based on the streak and schedules spaced reviews. In real time, the AI only rewords explanations, with caching, validation and a model-free fallback if it fails.
psicoSprint.impact: In fifteen minutes candidates know where they stand, skill by skill, and get a plan that focuses on their weak points. Each session stores the seed and the versions of the engine and scoring, so any result can be reproduced and explained. Paid access is a one-off payment with no automatic renewal.

Results by skill with accuracy, speed and priority areas
Adaptive plan that adjusts difficulty and reinforces weak points
Timed mock exams and error review with explanations
Progress history and one-off 30-day or 180-day plans

faq.a: The skills are shared and can be trained today. Content specific to each force is being prepared; the platform flags this in each case.

sundayCampers.seoTitle: Sunday Campers: campervan hire website with bookings and SEO in 9 languages | IA Operators
sundayCampers.title: Sunday Campers: campervan hire website in Málaga with online booking
sundayCampers.h1: Website, bookings and performance for a campervan hire business in Málaga
sundayCampers.subtitle: Campervan hire · Málaga · 9 languages
sundayCampers.tagline: A site with real-time availability, online payment and routes across Andalusia in nine languages, optimised after a mobile performance audit that found where the seconds were being lost.
sundayCampers.serviceType: Web development, online booking and technical SEO
sundayCampers.problem: A campervan hire business sells mainly to foreign tourists comparing options on their phones, sometimes from abroad and in a hurry. It needs to show real availability, take payment without intermediaries and appear in several languages. The mobile audit in August 2026 showed that the main image took almost five seconds to render, not because of its size but because of avoidable waits.
sundayCampers.context: The audit broke the problem into measurable parts. 65% of the delay was time spent waiting for the main image to start loading, because the element did not exist until the page hydrated. On top of that came two analytics containers running in parallel, a redirect from the root to the Spanish version costing around 700 ms and images linked from third-party domains.
sundayCampers.engineeringIntro: The website is built with Next.js on Supabase and Stripe. Availability is read from a daily view per vehicle and synced with external calendars via iCal. The price is recalculated on the server before the payment is created, and the database itself prevents two bookings from overlapping. After the audit, each cause it found was fixed in the code, one by one.
sundayCampers.impact: The main image is now rendered on the server with high priority, a single analytics container remains and loads deferred, the root resolves with a rewrite instead of a redirect and all images are served from the site's own domain. The site still needs to be re-measured with the same method before the after figures are published; once they are, they will appear here with their date.

Calculates the price with extras and takes payment through Stripe Checkout
Syncs bookings from other channels via iCal
Publishes routes across Andalusia and vehicle pages in several languages
Offers direct WhatsApp contact from each vehicle page

faq.q: Why have the performance figures not been published yet?
faq.a: Because we only publish numbers measured with a stated method and date. The fixes are in the code; the new PageSpeed Insights measurement, using the median of several runs, will be published on this page once it is done.

faq.q: Why was the image size not the problem?
faq.a: Downloading the image took about 126 ms. The time went on waiting: almost 1.8 seconds before it started loading, because the element was not in the initial HTML, and another 0.8 seconds before it could be painted.

renuva.seoTitle: Renuva: extraordinary regularisation renewals for immigration law firms | IA Operators
renuva.title: Renuva: regularisation renewals, organised by firm
renuva.h1: A tool so that no client of the firm misses their renewal
renuva.subtitle: Immigration law firms · Extraordinary regularisation
renuva.tagline: An application for immigration law firms that manages each regularised client's renewal window, sends alerts by WhatsApp or email and collects documents through a multilingual portal.
renuva.serviceType: Management software for immigration law firms
renuva.problem: The extraordinary regularisation leaves each firm with dozens or hundreds of permits expiring on different dates. Each renewal has its own window: it opens before expiry, there is a grace period afterwards and, once that has passed, the client risks penalty proceedings. Tracking it in a spreadsheet works until someone misses a date.
renuva.engineeringIntro: Renuva is a multi-firm application on Next.js and Supabase, hosted in the European Union. The firm imports its client list from CSV or Excel, the system validates each NIE and works out the renewal window status for each case. Alerts go out through the official WhatsApp API when there is consent and an approved template, and by email otherwise. Clients upload their documents to a portal in Spanish, Arabic or French.
renuva.impact: The firm sees on a dashboard which renewals are open, which are in the grace period and which are out of time, and no longer chases each client by hand. Renuva is currently in a pilot phase: the document lists for each route need review by a lawyer and the Arabic and French translations are provisional before it opens to real firms.

faq.q: Does Renuva calculate the expiry date?
faq.a: No. The firm supplies the date from the decision or the TIE, and the system records where it came from. Renuva calculates the renewal window from that date, which is where things get forgotten.

faq.a: No. Renuva does not send data to any language model. The deadline and alert rules are written and tested.

verifactuKit.seoTitle: VERI*FACTU Readiness Kit: decide before you switch software | IA Operators
verifactuKit.title: VERI*FACTU Readiness Kit for the self-employed and SMEs
verifactuKit.h1: A kit to decide what to do about VERI*FACTU before paying for it
verifactuKit.subtitle: Self-employed and SMEs on standard software · One-off payment
verifactuKit.tagline: A paid digital product with nine modules to find out whether VERI*FACTU applies to you, what to ask your software provider and which records to keep, before switching software or hiring an integration.
verifactuKit.problem: A self-employed professional or a small business hears about VERI*FACTU, Spain's new invoicing software rules, and does not know whether it applies, from when, or whether their invoicing software already handles it. Most answers come from people selling software, and the timetable has already moved more than once. With that much noise, the usual outcome is to put the decision off or to switch software for no reason.
verifactuKit.context: The Kit sits in the middle of IA Operators' VERI*FACTU funnel: free content, an indicative test, the paid Kit, a technical audit and, only when needed, an integration project. It is built for people on standard software. Anyone with their own ERP, POS or e-commerce needs something else, and the Kit tells them when.
verifactuKit.engineeringIntro: The Kit is sold through Stripe and delivered by magic link, with no passwords. The paid content lives only on the server and is served after checking, on every request, that the order is paid, active and within its access period. The buyer's progress, on the other hand, stays in their browser: the Kit does not need to store it on any server to work. Regulatory dates come from a single data module, the same one the rest of the VERI*FACTU section uses.
verifactuKit.impact: The buyer ends up with an indicative answer on whether it applies, fifteen closed questions for their provider, a matrix to compare alternatives, two emails ready to send and a four-week plan. They also know what the Kit does not do: it does not issue invoices, does not send records to the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) and does not certify compliance.

faq.a: It helps you understand the problem, but it does not solve it. One module explains when an ERP, a POS, an e-commerce store or vertical software needs technical work. In those cases the next step is an audit, not a kit.
